58.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.

1. Definitions
1.1. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.

1.4. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.5. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.6. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Subrogation
3.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
3.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

4. Complaints
4.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
4.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
4.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

5. Market conditions
5.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

6. Therapy Services
6.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
6.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
6.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
6.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

7. Dental Care
7.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
7.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
7.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
7.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
7.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
7.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

8. Geographical limits
8.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
8.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

9. Arbitration
9.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
9.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

10. Claims documents
10.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
10.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

11. Appeals
11.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
11.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
11.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

12. Optional cover: Hearing Care
12.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
12.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
12.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
12.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

13. Customer support
13.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
13.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

14. General exclusions
14.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
14.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
14.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

15. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)

§ 18  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 19  Theft
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

§ 20  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 21  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(2) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 22  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 23  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 24  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 25  Compensation scheme
(1) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 26  Cooperation
(1) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

§ 27  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 28  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 29  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 30  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 31  Records and evidence
(1) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 32  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

§ 33  Freezer contents
(1) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(2) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

§ 34  Salvage
(1) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

§ 35  Making a claim
(1) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(2) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

§ 36  Garden and outdoor cover
(1) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

§ 37  Cancellation
(1) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(2) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(3) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

§ 7  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

§ 8  Making a claim
(1) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 9  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 10  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 11  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 12  Claims documents
(1) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(2) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 13  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 14  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 15  Compensation scheme
(1) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 16  Salvage
(1) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

§ 17  Locks and keys
(1) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $750 for any one claim.

§ 18  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 19  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

§ 20  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 21  Cooperation
(1) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

§ 22  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 23  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 24  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 25  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 26  Alternative accommodation
(1) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(2) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(3) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

§ 27  Tenant's improvements
(1) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(2) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

§ 28  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 29  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 30  Freezer contents
(1) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(2) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

§ 31  Complaints
(1) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 4

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.11. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.12. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.13. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.14. Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.15. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.16. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.17. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Therapy Services
3.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
3.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
3.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

4. Vision Care
4.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
4.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
4.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
4.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
5.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
5.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

6. Dental Care
6.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
6.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
6.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
6.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
6.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
6.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

8. Making a claim
8.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

9. Salvage
9.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
9.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

10. Wellness allowance
10.1. Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
10.2. The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

11. Electronic documents

11.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
11.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

12. Change of address

12.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

19.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

20.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.

21. Governing law

22. Inflation
22.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.

23. Complaints
23.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
23.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.

(2) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(3) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(4) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

§ 10  Interest

(1) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
(2) Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

§ 12  Communication
(1) The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
(2) The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 13  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

(1) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

(1) The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.

(1) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.

§ 18  Dependants

(2) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

§ 19  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 20  Assignment
(1) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

§ 21  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 22  Salvage
(1) When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

§ 23  Arbitration
(1) If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

§ 24  Leaving the plan
(1) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(2) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

§ 25  Sanctions
(1) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 26  Records and evidence
(1) The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 27  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
(2) The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

§ 28  Cooperation
(1) The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

§ 29  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 30  Premium payment
(1) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 31  Claims documents
(1) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(2) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 32  Third-party administrators
(1) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(2) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 33  Data protection
(1) The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

§ 34  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

§ 35  Coordination of benefits
(1) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(2) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

§ 36  Inflation
(1) The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 37  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 38  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 39  Waiver
(1) If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 40  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 41  Notices
(1) Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
(2) Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 42  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 43  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

(1) If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

(1) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(2) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

§ 46  Renewal
(1) The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.

(2) The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

INDEPENDENT DEVELOPMENT CASE
RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(2) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(3) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(4) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(5) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(6) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(7) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(8) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(9) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(10) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(11) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(12) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(13) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(2) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(3) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(4) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(5) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Flood
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

§ 4  Escape of Water
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

§ 5  Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(1) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

§ 6  Theft
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

§ 7  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

§ 8  Making a claim
(1) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 9  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 10  Change of address
(1) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 11  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 12  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 13  Compensation scheme
(1) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 14  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(2) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 15  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 16  Premium payment
(1) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 17  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

§ 18  Complaints
(1) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 19  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 20  Garden and outdoor cover
(1) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

§ 21  Locks and keys
(1) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $750 for any one claim.

§ 22  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 23  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 24  Cancellation
(1) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(2) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(3) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

§ 25  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(2) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

§ 26  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 27  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 28  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

§ 29  Inflation
(1) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 30  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 31  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 32  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 33  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 34  Electronic documents
(1) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(2) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 35  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 36  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 37  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 38  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 39  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 40  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(2) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(3) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(4) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(5) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(6) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(7) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(8) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(9) Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
(10) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(11) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(12) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(13) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(14) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

§ 2  Limits and deductible
(1) Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(2) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(3) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(4) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(5) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

§ 3  Therapy Services
(1) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(2) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
(3) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(4) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

§ 4  Dental Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(4) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(5) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(6) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

§ 5  Vision Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(2) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(3) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(4) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

§ 6  Optional cover: Hearing Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(3) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
(4) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

(1) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(2) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(3) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(4) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(5) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

(1) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(3) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

(1) Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
(2) Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

(3) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

(2) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 12  Wellness allowance
(1) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(2) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

§ 13  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 14  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 15  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.

§ 19  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.

§ 20  Third-party administrators
(1) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.

(2) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

(1) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.

(1) When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.

(1) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

§ 29  Leaving the plan

(6) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
(7) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(8) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(2) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(3) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(4) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(5) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Rental car excess
(1) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(2) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

§ 4  Baggage and Personal Belongings
(1) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

§ 5  Trip Cancellation
(1) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

§ 6  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 7  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(2) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

§ 8  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 9  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 10  Emergency Medical Expenses
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

§ 11  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 12  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

§ 13  Making a claim
(1) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(3) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(2) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(3) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(4) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(5) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(6) Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(7) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(8) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(9) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(10) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(11) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(12) Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
(13) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
(14) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(15) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(16) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(17) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(18) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

§ 2  Limits and deductible
(1) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(2) Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(3) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(4) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(5) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Dependants
(1) The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
(2) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

§ 4  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

§ 5  Waiver
(1) If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 6  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(2) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 7  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 8  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 9  Records and evidence
(1) The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 10  Electronic documents
(1) The Plan will send documents by email unless the Member asks for paper copies.
(2) The Member must tell the Plan if the Member's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 11  Eligibility
(1) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
(2) Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

§ 12  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 13  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 14  Vision Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(2) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(3) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(4) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

§ 15  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 16  Salvage
(1) When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

§ 17  Dental Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
(4) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(5) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(6) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

§ 18  Interest
(1) The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 19  Therapy Services
(1) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(2) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
(3) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(4) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

§ 20  Notices
(1) Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
(2) Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 21  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 22  Wellness allowance
(1) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(2) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

§ 23  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 24  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 25  Subrogation
(1) The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 26  Change of address
(1) The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
(2) The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 27  Appeals
(1) If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
(2) An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
(3) The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

§ 28  Assignment
(1) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

§ 29  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 30  Payment of claims
(1) The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
(2) The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

§ 31  Compensation scheme
(1) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 32  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 33  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 34  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 35  Automatic renewal
(1) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
(2) The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

§ 36  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

§ 37  Third-party administrators
(1) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(2) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 38  Optional cover: Hearing Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(3) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
(4) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

§ 39  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 40  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
(2) The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

§ 41  Complaints
(1) If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 42  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 43  Inflation
(1) The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 44  General exclusions
(1) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(2) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(3) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(4) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.

§ 45  Arbitration
(1) If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

§ 46  Premium payment
(1) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 47  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 48  Data protection
(1) The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

§ 49  Sanctions
(1) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 50  Communication
(1) The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
(2) The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 51  Renewal
(1) The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 52  Leaving the plan
(1) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(2) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

§ 53  Customer support
(1) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

§ 54  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 55  Making a claim
(1) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 56  Claims documents
(1) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(2) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 57  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 58  Cooperation
(1) The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

§ 59  Coordination of benefits
(1) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(2) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

§ 60  Cancellation
(1) The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(2) After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(3) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

(3) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 4  Complaints
(1) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.

(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

(1) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

(1) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.

(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

(1) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 45  Automatic renewal
(1) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(2) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

§ 46  Contents temporarily removed
(1) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(2) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

§ 47  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(2) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

§ 48  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 49  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 50  Electronic documents
(1) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(2) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 51  Flood
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.

(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 53  Environmental commitment

(2) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 54  Tenant's improvements
(1) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
