1.21. Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.22. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Trip Cancellation
3.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
3.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. Emergency Medical Expenses
5.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
5.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
5.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
5.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
5.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

6. Optional cover: Travel Delay
6.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
6.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

8. Making a claim
8.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

9. Claims documents
9.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
9.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

10. Change of address
10.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
10.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

11. Rental car excess
11.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
11.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

12. How to read this document
12.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
12.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
12.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

13. Electronic documents
13.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
13.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
13.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

14. Compensation scheme
14.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
14.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

15. Premium payment
15.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
15.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

16. Reasonable precautions
16.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
16.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

17. Changes in circumstances
17.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
17.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

18. Missed departure
18.1. We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
18.2. You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

19. Discounts
19.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
19.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

20. Notices
20.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
20.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

21. Duty of fair presentation
21.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
21.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
21.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

22. Fraud
22.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
22.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

23. Automatic renewal
23.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
23.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

24. Environmental commitment
24.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
24.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

25. Records and evidence
25.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
25.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
25.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

26. Geographical limits
26.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
26.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

27. Accessibility
27.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

28. Recovery of costs
28.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

29. Currency
29.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
29.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

30. Cancellation
30.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
30.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
30.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

31. Severability
31.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

32. Joint policyholders
32.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
32.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

33. Cooperation
33.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
33.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
34.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

35. Personal liability
35.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
35.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
35.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

36. Arbitration
36.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
36.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

37. Interest
37.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

38. Subrogation
38.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
38.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

39. Emergency assistance
39.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
39.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
39.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

40. Market conditions
40.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

41. Sanctions
41.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

42. Payment of claims
42.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
42.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

43. Data protection
43.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
43.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
43.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

44. Customer support
44.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
44.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

45. Repatriation
45.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
45.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

46. Assignment
46.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

47. Communication
47.1. We will communicate with you in English.
47.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

48. Complaints
48.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
48.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
48.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

49. Salvage
49.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
49.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

50. Renewal
50.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
50.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

51. Taxes
51.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
51.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

52. Interpretation
52.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
52.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
52.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

53. Third-party administrators
53.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
53.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

54. Legal expenses abroad
54.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
54.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

55. Inflation
55.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
55.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

56. Other insurance
56.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
56.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

57. Governing law
57.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
57.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

58. Waiver
58.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

59. Exchange of information
59.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
59.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

60. Instalment agreements
60.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
60.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(2) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(3) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(4) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(2) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(3) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(4) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(5) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

§ 3  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 4  Change of address
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 5  Arbitration
(1) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

§ 6  Optional cover: Travel Delay
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

§ 7  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

§ 8  Trip Cancellation
(1) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

§ 9  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 10  Legal expenses abroad
(1) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(2) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

§ 11  Personal liability
(1) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(2) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

§ 12  Communication
(1) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(2) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 13  Inflation
(1) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 14  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 15  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 16  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

§ 17  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 18  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 19  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 20  Assignment
(1) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

§ 21  Making a claim
(1) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(2) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(3) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

§ 22  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.
